title: Modeling of DNA Damage Repair and Cell Response in Relation to p53 System Exposed to Ionizing Radiation.
authors: Hu, Ankang; Zhou, Wanyi; Wu, Zhen; Zhang, Hui; Li, Junli; Qiu, Rui
one_liner_zh: 该文用蒙特卡洛模拟结合p53系统模型研究辐射诱导DNA损伤修复动力学，虽涉及DNA修复与p53互作，但非蛋白质-DNA结合识别或TF-DNA互作建模，且方法为辐射生物效应模拟，与课题核心关联弱。
abstract: Repair of DNA damage induced by ionizing radiation plays an important role in the cell response to ionizing radiation. Radiation-induced DNA damage also activates the p53 system, which determines the fate of cells. The kinetics of repair, which is affected by the cell itself and the complexity of DNA damage, influences the cell response and fate via affecting the p53 system. To mechanistically study the influences of the cell response to different LET radiations, we introduce a new repair module and a p53 system model with NASIC, a Monte Carlo track structure code. The factors determining the kinetics of the double-strand break (DSB) repair are modeled, including the chromosome environment and complexity of DSB. The kinetics of DSB repair is modeled considering the resection-dependent and resection-independent compartments. The p53 system is modeled by simulating the interactions among genes and proteins. With this model, the cell responses to low- and high-LET irradiation are simulated, respectively. It is found that the kinetics of DSB repair greatly affects the cell fate and later biological effects. A large number of DSBs and a slow repair process lead to severe biological consequences. High-LET radiation induces more complex DSBs, which can be repaired by slow processes, subsequently resulting in a longer cycle arrest and, furthermore, apoptosis and more secreting of TGFbeta. The Monte Carlo track structure simulation with a more realistic repair module and the p53 system model developed in this study can expand the functions of the NASIC code in simulating mechanical radiobiological effects.
abstract_zh: 电离辐射诱导的DNA损伤修复在细胞对电离辐射的响应中扮演重要角色。辐射诱导的DNA损伤也激活p53系统，该系统决定细胞的命运。修复动力学受细胞自身及DNA损伤复杂性的影响，并通过影响p53系统进而影响细胞响应和命运。为机制性研究细胞对不同线性能量转移（LET）辐射的响应影响，我们引入了一个新的修复模块和一个结合NASIC（一种蒙特卡洛径迹结构代码）的p53系统模型。决定双链断裂（DSB）修复动力学的因素被建模，包括染色体环境和DSB的复杂性。DSB修复动力学通过考虑依赖切除和不依赖切除的区室进行建模。p53系统通过模拟基因和蛋白质之间的相互作用来建模。利用该模型，分别模拟了细胞对低和高LET辐射的响应。研究发现，DSB修复动力学显著影响细胞命运及后续生物效应。大量DSB和缓慢的修复过程导致严重的生物后果。高LET辐射诱导更复杂的DSB，这些DSB可通过缓慢过程修复，随后导致更长的周期阻滞，进而引发凋亡和更多TGFbeta的分泌。本研究开发的具有更现实修复模块和p53系统模型的蒙特卡洛径迹结构模拟，可扩展NASIC代码在模拟机械性放射生物学效应方面的功能。
